title: Property Contracting Note: Several Hotel Reservations Held at Once
content:
A guest may hold any number of Hotel Rate Plans reservations at the same time, including several at the same property on overlapping dates, and each reservation carries its own rate plan and its own folio. No ceiling is placed on the number a guest may hold.

**1. Duplicates at one property.** Where two reservations at the same property overlap in dates and name the same lead guest, the later reservation is opened and then referred for duplicate review, because properties treat duplicate rooms as a single guarantee. The match that raises the review is the property: two reservations at different properties over the same dates are not duplicates of one another.

**2. Rooms stay where they were booked.** Rooms are never moved between reservations. A guest who wants fewer rooms gives up the rooms on the reservation they stand on, and each room follows that reservation's own rate plan.

**3. One reservation, one plan.** Rate plans are never mixed on one reservation; a guest who wants different terms for different rooms holds two reservations.

## The rule applied to combinations

| Two reservations, same lead guest | Same property | Dates overlap | What follows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | yes | the later reservation is opened, and is then referred for duplicate review |
| yes | yes | no | both stand; no duplicate review arises on this ground |
| yes | no | yes | both stand; no duplicate review arises on this ground |

## A question this note answers

*A guest holds one reservation on the Standard Flexible Rate and wants two of its four rooms on the Member Flex Rate instead.* One reservation carries one rate plan, so the two sets of terms cannot sit on a single reservation; a second reservation is what holds the different terms, and the rooms are not moved across from the first.
